facts.statement: The only known species, Miosynechodus mora, was named in 1969.
facts.quote: A single species is known, Miosynechodus mora, which was named in 1969.

facts.statement: Originally thought to be a fin spine from a hybodontid shark, it is now classified as a tail stinger from a myliobatiform ray.
facts.quote: It was originally identified as a fin spine from a late-surviving hybodontid, but it is now considered to be a myliobatiform tail stinger.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a single tail stinger found in the personal collection of Deraniyagala.
facts.quote: The holotype of Miosynechodus is a single tail stinger from Deraniyagala's personal collection.

facts.statement: The holotype measures 41 mm in length, 10 mm in width, and 6 mm in depth, featuring five longitudinal grooves.
facts.quote: It measures 41 mm in overall length, with a width of 10 mm and a depth of 6 mm, and has five longitudinal grooves.

facts.statement: This genus lived during the Langhian stage, between 15.98 and 13.82 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Langhian to Langhian (15.98 to 13.82 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists Hybodontidae as the parent group for Miosynechodus.
Miosynechodus is classified within the family Hybodontidae.
Miosynechodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Miosynechodus mora is the type species for the genus Miosynechodus.
Miosynechodus is considered a dubious genus of an extinct ray from the Miocene of Sri Lanka.
facts.quote: Miosynechodus is a dubious genus of extinct ray from the Miocene of Sri Lanka.
